body.estimand_functional: \(\bigl[\text{for every }N\geq2\text{ and feasible }\mathbf n,\quad\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\bigr]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C^{\mathsf T}WC\in\mathcal R_K\)

sampling_model.design: The main cone and Loewner theorems use a uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law: every arm count \(n_a\) is positive, \(\sum_a n_a\leq N\), and the remaining \(n_\circ=N-\sum_a n_a\) units receive an explicit unassigned label. Balance, exhaustive assignment, and divisibility of \(N\) are not required. Separately, the general nonexchangeable-kernel theorem ranges only over \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), whose support has \(n=N/K\) units per arm and no unassigned units.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object. For the headline it is uniform on the stated arbitrary fixed-count support; for the separate kernel characterization it follows a known admissible balanced nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every treatment arm has known positive marginal probability \(n_a/N>0\). The unassigned probability \(n_\circ/N\) may equal zero. On the balanced-kernel subdomain, every arm marginal is \(1/K\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural endpoint conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\). The Aronow--Green--Lee recovery is therefore a finite oracle equality; consistency and asymptotic behavior of an endpoint estimated from observed margins are outside this theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The binary sample-and-assign oracle variance has a sharp upper endpoint attained by comonotone potential outcomes, allowing an unassigned remainder.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under any uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design with arbitrary positive arm counts and an optional unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. The completion-dependent term is count-invariant and retains the exact \(2/N\) regret coefficient, so the certificate needs no balance, exhaustive assignment, or divisibility condition. The full finite binary oracle design of Aronow, Green, and Lee is recovered, including unassigned units and the normalization \(S=N\sigma_N/(N-1)\); this is distinct from their estimated-bound asymptotics. The exact copositivity characterization for general nonexchangeable kernels remains on its separate balanced exhaustive subdomain, while polynomial recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee give the sharp binary oracle endpoint for a sampled experiment, and Zhao and Ding give multi-arm complete-randomization covariance algebra. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion is universally least favourable for every uniform multi-arm fixed-count sample-and-assign design, including unequal allocations and unassigned units. On the separate realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone whose validity is invariant across all uniform fixed-count vectors, plus a sharper Loewner classification. The broader uniform-design theorem is kept distinct from the exact cut-copositivity representation on the balanced nonexchangeable moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact arbitrary-count sample-and-assign covariance decomposition, proves that the graph-Laplacian equivalence, binary necessity witness, \(2/N\) regret identity, and Loewner boundary require neither balance nor exhaustive assignment, and recovers the full finite Aronow--Green--Lee oracle formula. The \(K=3,N=6\) calculations remain exact balanced special-case audits with \(n_a=2\) and \(n_\circ=0\). For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the project preserves the finite cut-copositivity characterization and exact algebraic algorithm while leaving polynomial complexity and the minimal complete alphabet as explicit residual questions.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee analyze \(N\geq4\) fixed units, a simple random sample of source size \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\), and exactly \(m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\) treated and \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\) controls. The binary recovery proposition matches their finite oracle design and Lemma 1 term by term after \(S=N\sigma_N/(N-1)\), and proves the common-rank sharp endpoint; it does not claim their estimated-bound asymptotics. Imbens and Menzel use isotone completion for a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance algebra but do not optimize the unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular order is consistent with the rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here is finite. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. use integer programming. The separate general-kernel theorem remains restricted to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result does not supply the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate covers uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign laws and a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not cover arbitrary nonexchangeable assignment probabilities or turn the endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. The separate balanced-kernel copositivity theorem remains exhaustive but factorial or exponential in its direct enumeration, and its strict witnesses may require as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm. It therefore does not settle polynomial-time recognition or binary-witness completeness.
body.honest_scope: The uniform fixed-count cone theorem follows from exact design inclusion-probability algebra plus a finite rearrangement proof and a contrast-geometry necessity classification; novelty lies in the count-invariant causal contrast boundary and Loewner characterization, not in a new general dependence inequality. The Aronow--Green--Lee comparison is an exact finite oracle recovery under their stated \(N,n_{\mathrm{AGL}},m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\) restrictions, not an estimated-bound asymptotic result. The six-unit propositions remain audit certificates. The nonexchangeable-kernel contribution is separately confined to balanced exhaustive laws and consists of the exact cut-copositivity equivalence and a terminating algorithm only for exact real-algebraic inputs. No algebraic enumeration is claimed for unrestricted real inputs, and no polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: For every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner needs only inspect the off-diagonal signs of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\): nonpositive signs certify one-sort least-favourable completion, and any positive sign identifies two arms on which a binary reversal strictly improves the loss. This certificate and its \(2/N\) regret identity are unchanged by unequal arm sizes or unassigned units. Matrix-valued conservativeness remains much rarer and occurs only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. Under a nonexchangeable balanced design, the analogous exact question is instead a finite family of copositivity tests after choosing a common unit order; this is decidable for exact algebraic inputs but is not yet a scalable certificate.
